BREAKING: Elon Musk says Grok 4.5 is now in private beta at SpaceX and Tesla.

Built on the 1.5T V9 foundation model with supplemental training using Cursor data, early evaluations show performance close to, or possibly beyond, Opus.

Musk also said reinforcement learning continues to improve the model and the Grok team is actively pushing performance even higher.

This isn’t just a vehicle manual.
It’s Tesla building the complete safety and operational infrastructure needed for real-world unsupervised Robotaxi service.
The level of thought that went into how the car itself should behave in emergencies is impressive.
Full document here:
digitalassets.tesla.com/tesl…
What’s your biggest takeaway from this? 👇

High-voltage disable procedure:
Open the hood and double-cut the dedicated “First Responder Loop”, then double-cut the negative low-voltage cable. Wait 2 minutes for full de-power.
A QR code on the bottom left of the windshield links directly to this plan.

First responder support tools built into the vehicle:
•  Dedicated 24/7 Tesla Robotaxi First Responder Support line: (512) 276-5391
•  On-board two-way communication (microphones on B-pillars + cabin + underside speakers)
•  First responders can request a temporary 1,000 ft geofence around an incident so other Robotaxis stay out of the area

Automatic behavior after a collision or airbag deployment:
The Cybercab will:
•  Stop and park itself
•  Disable autonomy
•  Rapidly flash hazard lights
•  Automatically unlock the doors
•  Roll the windows down (if airbags deployed)
•  Initiate two-way voice communication with Tesla Support
•  Stay stationary until the situation is resolved

Hazard lights are the key signal:
•  Normal flash rate during pickup and drop-off
•  Rapid flashing (roughly 2x the normal speed) when Autonomous Mode is disabled or after a safety-critical event
This rapid flashing is the main visual cue that it’s safe to approach the vehicle.
